definition: A division into two branches or divergent developmental lineages in stem cell trajectory modeling.
etymology: From New Latin bifurcatio, from Latin bi- ('two') + furca ('fork').
manuscriptExample: Single-cell pseudotime analysis identified a critical transcriptional bifurcation governing myeloid versus lymphoid fate.
conferenceExample: We addressed the reviewer's query regarding marker gene expression prior to cell lineage bifurcation.

definition: The proportion of a drug or biomarker that enters systemic circulation and reaches the active site.
manuscriptExample: Liposomal encapsulation increased oral bioavailability of the small-molecule inhibitor by four-fold.
conferenceExample: The panel requested pharmacokinetic curves demonstrating adequate target tissue bioavailability.
